stories.title: Initialize Rust workspace with all crate stubs and tooling
stories.description:
Create the Rust workspace skeleton for all SCP crates. Pure scaffolding — no business logic, no trait definitions. Directory structure, Cargo.toml files with ALL dependencies declared, empty module stubs, and tooling config.

Layout follows `.docs/scaffold/rust.md`. Standards from `.docs/standards/rust.md`: edition 2024, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on every crate, workspace-level clippy lints.

Declare ALL workspace dependencies upfront in `[workspace.dependencies]` so no subsequent story needs to modify any Cargo.toml. Individual crates reference these with `dep.workspace = true`.

All module stubs are valid empty Rust modules with `//!` doc comments. Parent mod.rs files declare all sub-modules with `pub mod` so downstream stories populate child files without touching parents.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` produces zero warnings
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
Workspace root Cargo.toml has resolver="2", members: scp-core, scp-transport, scp-platform, scp-testing
[workspace.package] sets edition="2024"

[workspace.dependencies] declares: openmls, tokio, serde, serde_json, thiserror, ed25519-dalek, x25519-dalek, pkarr, z-base-32, sha2, hmac, hkdf, aes-gcm, rmp-serde, rand, rand_chacha, futures, tracing, tracing-subscriber, tokio-tungstenite, async-trait, proptest (dev)
[workspace.lints.clippy] sets: all=warn, pedantic=warn, nursery=warn, cargo=warn, unwrap_used=deny, expect_used=deny, panic=deny
Every crate lib.rs has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`

stories.title: Define platform abstraction traits and supporting types
stories.description:
Define the four platform abstraction traits and all supporting types in `crates/scp-platform/src/traits.rs`. The trait signatures MUST match ADR-006 acceptance criteria 5 exactly.

Key constraints:
- `KeyHandle` is opaque: `pub struct KeyHandle(pub(crate) u64)` — pub(crate) lets testing adapters create handles.
- All traits are `Send + Sync` bounded.
- Use `#[async_trait]` for object safety (`Box<dyn KeyCustody>` must work).
- `derive_pseudonym` doc comment must specify the exact algorithm: HMAC-SHA256(key_material, context_id || "scp-pseudonym") -> Ed25519_keygen(seed[0..32]).

Update lib.rs to `pub mod traits; pub use traits::*;`.

stories.title: Implement DID creation, verification, and DidMethod trait
stories.description:
Implement DID creation per ADR-003. This is local-only — no DHT publishing or resolution (that's SCP-005).

`create_identity(key_custody)` generates three keypairs: Identity Key (Ed25519, derives DID string), Active Signing Key (Ed25519, rotatable), Pre-Rotation Key (Ed25519, commitment only). DID string: `did:dht:` + z-base-32(identity_key.public). Constructs DID Document with verification methods.

`verify_did(did_string, public_key)` is a local self-certification check: decode z-base-32 suffix, compare to public key.

`DidMethod` trait abstracts the DID method. `DidDht` implements it.

ScpIdentity struct holds: identity_key (KeyHandle), active_signing_key (KeyHandle), pre_rotation_commitment ([u8;32]), did (String).

DID Document: standard W3C format with verification methods #0 (identity), #active (signing), PreRotationCommitment service.

stories.title: Implement DID publishing and resolution via Mainline DHT
stories.description:
Implement publish_did_document and resolve_did per ADR-003 criteria 2-3.

`publish_did_document(identity)`: publish DID Document to Mainline DHT as BEP44 signed mutable item via pkarr. Monotonically increasing sequence number. Idempotent.

Republishing strategy: background tokio task every 2 hours. Exponential backoff on failure (30s→30m cap). DhtPublishDegraded warning after 6 failures. Auto-start on identity load, stop on unload.

`resolve_did(did_string)`: resolve via DHT lookup. Verify self-certification (z-base-32 matches key). Verify BEP44 signature. Cache results: 24h refresh for active, 7d for inactive. Return staleness indicator.

Resolution cache in identity/cache.rs: TTL-based, BEP44 sequence comparison.

stories.title: Implement DID key rotation and identity migration
stories.description:
Implement ADR-003 criteria 4a-4c: the three-layer key rotation architecture.

**Layer 1 — rotate_active_key**: Generate new Active Signing Key. Update DID Document (new verification method, retire old as #retired-{seq}). Sign with Identity Key. Publish to DHT with incremented sequence. DID string does NOT change.

**Layer 2 — migrate_identity**: Create new DID using pre-rotation key. Link old → new DID via alsoKnownAs. Old Identity Key signs new. Publish both documents. Return DidRotationEvent.

**Layer 3 — verify_migration**: Verify cryptographic linkage (old key signed new key). Verify pre-rotation proof if present (SHA-256 commitment match). Return strong/moderate assurance level.

Define DidRotationEvent, MigrationProof, PreRotationProof structs per ADR-003.

After rotation, DID Document has new #active method and retired old key
migrate_identity returns new Identity with different DID string
Old DID Document has alsoKnownAs pointing to new DID
verify_migration returns true for valid migration proof
verify_migration with pre-rotation proof provides strong assurance

stories.title: Implement MLS encrypt and decrypt with replay prevention
stories.description:
Implement ADR-001 criteria 4-5.

**encrypt(group, plaintext)**: encrypt as MLS PrivateMessage (application message). Ciphertext includes membership_tag HMAC (§9.8.1 inner check). MLS assigns generation number automatically (§9.8.2 layer a).

**decrypt(group, ciphertext)**: decrypt MLS PrivateMessage. Verify membership_tag — reject if sender is not valid group member. Verify generation number — reject if <= highest seen for this sender in this epoch (replay prevention). Return decrypted plaintext.

Generation number tracking: maintain per-sender, per-epoch highest-seen counter. Reject out-of-order duplicates.

Generation number tracking is per-sender per-epoch

stories.title: Implement MLS epoch ratcheting with EpochGraceStore and update proposals
stories.description:
Implement ADR-001 criteria 6-7.

**ratchet(group, commit)**: process Commit, advance to new epoch. Old epoch keys enter grace window. Grace window closes when: (a) all members sent in new epoch, or (b) 30 seconds (hard ceiling). After grace closes, old keys destroyed — forward secrecy. Messages arriving after grace are unrecoverable → emit StaleEpochMessage event.

**EpochGraceStore** (epoch_grace.rs): in-memory only, indexed by epoch number, auto-purged by timer. NOT accessible to any code path other than decrypt with matching epoch. Uses tokio::time::sleep for 30s ceiling.

**update(group)**: issue MLS Update proposal — fresh HPKE keypair, ratchet sender's tree path. Post-compromise security. Returns (UpdateProposal, Commit).

Old epoch keys are retained during 30-second grace window
decrypt with old epoch key succeeds during grace window
decrypt with old epoch key fails after grace window closes
StaleEpochMessage event emitted for messages after grace
EpochGraceStore is in-memory only, not persisted

After update is processed, old state compromise doesn't affect new messages

stories.title: Define envelope structs, bucket padding, and serialization
stories.description:
Define the two-layer envelope format per ADR-002. Struct definitions, MessagePack serialization, and bucket padding. No encryption/signing logic yet (those are SCP-012/013).

**InnerEnvelope** (inner.rs): context_id, sender_did, epoch, generation, sequence, timestamp, payload_hash ([u8;32]), payload (Vec<u8>), provenance (Option<Provenance>), signature ([u8;64]).

**OuterEnvelope** (outer.rs): routing_id ([u8;32]), recipient_hint (Option<[u8;32]>), blob_ttl (u32), encrypted_blob (Vec<u8>). create_outer_envelope constructor.

**Bucket padding** (padding.rs): buckets 256B, 1KB, 4KB, 16KB, 64KB, 256KB. pad_to_bucket appends padding + 4-byte big-endian original length suffix. strip_padding reads length suffix, truncates. Padding format: payload || padding_bytes || length_u32_be.

All structs derive Serialize/Deserialize for MessagePack via rmp-serde. Proptest for padding roundtrip.

stories.title: Implement pseudonym derivation and inner envelope creation with signing
stories.description:
Implement ADR-002 criteria 1-2, 6.

**derive_pseudonym(key_custody, identity_key_handle, context_id)**: delegates to key_custody.derive_pseudonym. Deterministic: same key + context = same pseudonym. Different context = different, unlinkable pseudonym. The pseudonym public key is the routing_id for outer envelopes.

**create_inner_envelope(...)**: compute payload_hash = SHA-256(payload) BEFORE padding. Compute provenance_hash = SHA-256(serialize(provenance)) or SHA-256(0x00) if absent. Sign: Ed25519_sign(SHA-256(context_id || sender_did || epoch || generation || sequence || timestamp || payload_hash || provenance_hash)). Pad payload AFTER signing. Return complete InnerEnvelope.

**verify_inner_signature(inner_envelope, sender_public_key)**: recompute hash, verify Ed25519 signature. Reject if mismatch (payload or provenance tampered).

stories.title: Implement envelope seal and open pipeline
stories.description:
Implement ADR-002 criteria 4-5, 7: the high-level send/receive pipeline.

**seal_envelope(inner_envelope, mls_group, routing_id, recipient_hint, blob_ttl)**: serialize inner envelope (MessagePack), encrypt via MLS, wrap in OuterEnvelope. This is the primary send path.

**open_envelope(outer_envelope, mls_group, sender_public_key)**: decrypt MLS layer, deserialize inner envelope, verify inner signature, verify payload_hash == SHA-256(stripped_payload). Reject on signature mismatch, hash mismatch, or MLS replay.

These functions compose ADR-001 (MLS encrypt/decrypt) with ADR-002 (envelope format) into a single call each.

stories.title: Implement pull-based sender key distribution protocol
stories.description:
Implement ADR-007 criteria 4a-4c: pull-based sender key distribution.

**Wire types** (MLS application messages):
- SenderKeyEpochAdvance: sender_did, epoch, signature (signs context_id || sender_did || "key_epoch" || epoch)
- SenderKeyRequest: requester_did, sender_did, epoch, wrapping_pubkey (X25519), signature
- SenderKeyResponse: sender_did, epoch, hpke_sealed_key, ephemeral_pubkey (X25519)

**publish_sender_key_epoch_advance**: sign and broadcast. O(1) cost.
**request_sender_key**: generate ephemeral X25519 wrapping key, sign request, send with recipient_hint. O(1).
**handle_sender_key_request**: verify signature, check block list, HPKE-encrypt sender key to requester's wrapping key. O(1).

HPKE assembly: ephemeral X25519 keypair → ECDH → HKDF → AES-128-GCM encrypt sender key. Ephemeral public in response.

stories.title: Implement block notification and sender key rotation for block
stories.description:
Implement ADR-007 criteria 5-6: blocking via sender key rotation.

**rotate_sender_key_for_block(mls_group, blocked_did)**: generate new sender key, increment epoch, publish SenderKeyEpochAdvance. Add blocked_did to block list. Non-blocked members request new key normally; blocked party's request gets no response.

**send_block_notification(key_custody, mls_group, context_id, blocked_did, blocker_did)**: send signed MLS application message. Signature: Ed25519_sign(SHA-256(context_id || "block" || blocker_did || blocked_did || timestamp)). On receipt, blocked party's client auto-rotates their sender key excluding the blocker. Mutual block completes in one round-trip.

Verification on receipt: check Ed25519 signature against blocker's known signing key from MLS LeafNode. Discard if invalid.

stories.title: Implement native relay server
stories.description:
Implement ADR-004 relay server: WebSocket store-and-forward.

**server.rs**: tokio + tokio-tungstenite WebSocket server. Accept connections at `wss://<host>/scp/v1`. Handle all 7 client message types. Subscription registry maps routing_id → set of subscriber connections. PUBLISH stores blob and delivers to matching subscribers (filter by recipient_hint if present). SUBSCRIBE with since= backfills stored blobs (oldest-first). Connection multiplexing: one WS supports multiple subscriptions.

**storage.rs**: BlobStore trait + InMemoryBlobStore. Keyed by (routing_id, blob_id). TTL tracking. Background task deletes expired blobs.

Server config: configurable bind address, max_blob_size (default 262144), max_blob_ttl (default 604800), max_subscriptions_per_connection (default 100), rate limits.

Relay is a dumb pipe: no blob inspection, no client auth, no content validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Relay server starts and accepts WebSocket connections
PUBLISH stores blob and returns OK with blob_id (SHA-256 of blob)
SUBSCRIBE streams new blobs matching routing_id to subscriber
SUBSCRIBE with since= backfills stored blobs oldest-first then emits backfill_complete
UNSUBSCRIBE stops delivery for that routing_id
QUERY returns stored blobs matching routing_id without creating subscription
DELETE removes blob (best-effort)
ACK is fire-and-forget (no response)
Expired blobs are cleaned up by background TTL task
PING returns PONG
Relay rejects blobs exceeding max_blob_size with ERR 4010
One connection supports multiple concurrent subscriptions

Implement InMemoryBlobStore with HashMap and TTL tracking
Implement relay server in server.rs with tokio-tungstenite
Implement message routing: deserialize → dispatch → serialize response
Implement subscription registry with routing_id → subscribers mapping
Implement TTL expiry background task
Implement PING/PONG keepalive
Write integration tests: publish then subscribe, backfill, expiry

stories.title: Implement relay client and NativeRelayAdapter
stories.description:
Implement ADR-004 client + ADR-005 adapter.

**client.rs**: WebSocket client using tokio-tungstenite. Connect to relay URL. Send ClientMessage, receive RelayMessage. Reconnection with exponential backoff (1s→30s cap). On reconnect, re-issue SUBSCRIBE with since = last stored_at - 5s overlap. PING every 30s keepalive. Deduplication by blob_id.

**adapter.rs**: NativeRelayAdapter implements TransportAdapter trait. Maps: send→PUBLISH, subscribe→SUBSCRIBE+stream, unsubscribe→UNSUBSCRIBE, query→QUERY, delete→DELETE. Converts RelayMessage::Blob into TransportEvent::Envelope (parse OuterEnvelope from blob bytes).
acceptanceCriteria: Client connects to relay via WebSocket
Client sends PUBLISH and receives OK with blob_id
Client SUBSCRIBE receives streamed blobs
Client reconnects with exponential backoff on disconnect
On reconnect, re-subscribes with since=last_stored_at - 5s
Client deduplicates by blob_id
Client sends PING every 30 seconds
NativeRelayAdapter implements TransportAdapter trait
adapter.send maps to PUBLISH
adapter.subscribe returns Stream<TransportEvent>
Integration test: adapter publish → adapter subscribe → receive matches

Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff
Implement keepalive PING every 30s
Implement blob_id deduplication cache
Implement NativeRelayAdapter in adapter.rs
Map all TransportAdapter methods to relay protocol operations
Write integration tests against the relay server from SCP-019

stories.title: Phase 1 end-to-end integration test
stories.description:
The ultimate Phase 1 acceptance criterion: a single test exercising all 7 ADRs.

1. Alice creates a did:dht identity (ADR-003) using in-memory key custody (ADR-006)
2. Bob creates a did:dht identity (ADR-003) using in-memory key custody (ADR-006)
3. Alice creates an MLS group (ADR-001)
4. Alice generates a sender key (ADR-007) and publishes epoch advance
5. Bob publishes KeyPackages (ADR-001)
6. Alice adds Bob to the group using his KeyPackage (ADR-001)
7. Bob requests and receives Alice's sender key (ADR-007)
8. Alice creates a message, encrypts with sender key (ADR-007), wraps in inner envelope (ADR-002), encrypts with MLS (ADR-001), wraps in outer envelope with pseudonym routing (ADR-002)
9. Alice sends the outer envelope via the native relay (ADR-004) using the transport trait (ADR-005)
10. Bob receives the outer envelope via relay subscription (ADR-004, ADR-005)
11. Bob decrypts MLS layer (ADR-001), decrypts sender key layer (ADR-007), verifies inner envelope signature (ADR-002)
12. Bob reads Alice's message — it matches what Alice sent
13. Assert: the relay never saw Alice's DID, Bob's DID, the context ID, or message content

Run relay server in-process as a tokio task. Use localhost WebSocket.
acceptanceCriteria: Test runs end-to-end without manual intervention
Alice's message arrives at Bob intact after full encrypt/decrypt pipeline
MLS decryption succeeds (Bob is a valid group member)
Sender key decryption succeeds (Bob obtained Alice's sender key)
Inner envelope signature verification succeeds
payload_hash matches stripped payload after decryption
The relay server only handled opaque blobs — assert it never accessed plaintext
Routing was by pseudonym, not by DID
actionItems: Create phase1_integration.rs in scp-testing/tests/
Set up in-memory platform adapters for Alice and Bob
Create identities, MLS group, sender keys
Spawn relay server as tokio task on localhost
Connect Alice and Bob clients via NativeRelayAdapter
Execute the 13-step message exchange
Assert all verification steps pass
Assert relay opacity (only routing_id visible, content encrypted)

details.adr: Phase 1 Integration Test (end of ADR document)
details.notes: This test does NOT require DHT publishing — Alice and Bob share keys directly through the MLS group. DID resolution is not exercised. The test proves: identity works, encryption works, envelope format works, sender keys work, relay is a dumb pipe, transport abstraction is functional.
